title: deconflict-chatv1-param-aliasing-and-stream-fragment-reconcile-for-fncall-parity
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improve /v1/chat.completions parity: canonicalize parameter aliases (stop/stop_sequences/stop_array), normalize role aliases, add streaming fragment reconciliation for partial function-call payloads, and provide logprob fallbacks when streaming. Backwards compatible at API surface; no customer action required unless relying on non-standard aliases.
description:
Motivation and summary: The OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer has accumulated multiple overlapping parameter aliases and heuristics (stop, stop_sequences, stop_array, role aliases, etc.) and a couple of streaming corner cases where function-call payloads arrive in fragments and token-level logprobs are omitted. This PR unifies alias handling, documents canonical mappings, and adds a deterministic fragment reconciliation layer so streamed function calls reconstruct reliably even under partial/fuzzy framing.

Changes (high level):
- Canonical parameter mapping in the chatv1 adapter: accept legacy aliases (stop_sequences, stop_array, input_stop) and coerce them into a single internal "stop" array; emit deprecation warnings in logs for non-standard names.
- Role alias normalization: map role aliases such as "system_prompt" and "assistant_message" into canonical roles (system, assistant, user) and preserve any metadata via a new message.metadata map.
- Streaming fragment reconciliation: introduce monotonic fragment IDs and byte offsets on stream frames; implement a stitcher that can reassemble partial JSON fragments for function-call payloads, and fall back to sequence-based reordering when fragment IDs are missing. Heartbeat frames help detect mid-stream connection resets.
- Logprob fallback: when streaming mode omits per-token logprobs for performance, return a single-best-token summary at choice close; the API emits a backward-compatible choices[].logprobs_summary field.
- SDK and docs updates: small docs entry (docs/openai_parity.md) and the Python SDK adapter was adjusted to prefer the canonical names but preserve alias acceptance.

Checklist: 
- [x] Adapter mapping implemented and covered by unit tests
- [x] Stream fragment stitcher implemented and integration-tested against flaky ordering scenarios
- [x] Logprob fallback implemented and covered with a compatibility test suite
- [x] Docs updated with migration notes and examples
- [x] CI green after flake rerun

Compatibility notes: The adapter accepts both legacy aliases and the canonical names. Behavior is compatible with previous behavior except that ambiguous parameter combinations are resolved deterministically (the explicit canonical key wins). We log a deprecation message when aliases are used. Customers relying on ambiguous semantics should pin exact param names or validate on the SDK side.

Testing notes: Added unit tests for chatv1 param coercion and role normalization, and end-to-end integration tests that simulate reordered/fractured stream frames (including connection resumes) to validate the stitcher. Load test shows <1% p99 latency impact in common streaming paths.

Related work: ENG-2149 (param harmonization), ENG-2210 (stream resilience), SUP-402 (customer-reported fncall truncation incident).

Link to design doc: internal:docs/openai-compat/param-frag-reconcile (internal-only).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Please clarify how we resolve contradictory parameters if both 'stop' and 'stop_sequences' are provided. Maya: Resolved — canonical 'stop' wins. Added comment and unit test.

Liam O'Connor: Concerned about adding more fields to streaming frames increasing bandwidth. Maya: We only add a 16-byte fragment ID and 8-byte offset; benchmark shows negligible impact and much higher success for fncall reconstruction.
Sofia Martinez: Can we make the stitcher tolerant to duplicate fragments? Maya: Yes — stitcher dedups by fragment ID+offset; added tests for duplicates.
notes_for_release: Safe, backwards-compatible changes to chatv1 adapter and streaming; recommend customers to prefer 'stop' and 'role' canonical keys. No runtime flags needed.
